REF: PPR/2026 - 05/01
PUBLIC NOTICE ON CAP PRICES FOR PETROLEUM PRODUCTS EFFECTIVE
WEDNESDAY, 6th MAY 2026
The changes in fuel prices in the country for the month of May 2026 have been largely
influenced by the ongoing conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran, which
began on 28th February 2026.
Attacks on oil fields, storage facilities, and refineries, along with closure of the Strait of
Hormuz which handles approximately 20% of the world’s transported oil, have affected
oil production and supply from the Middle East where Tanzania sources most of its
products. This has equally increased shipping costs due to a shortage of cargo vessels
and raised insurance premiums for cargo ships.
The increase in fuel prices is a global crisis, and Tanzania, as part of this, is taking
various measures to ensure the security of fuel supply in the country and maintain
affordable prices to minimize economic and social impacts. In this regard, the
Government has provided a subsidy of TZS 259/litre to reduce the price of diesel, the
product used in major economic activities such as manufacturing, transportation of
products and public transport. In light of this situation and the ongoing conflict, which
has affected fuel infrastructure in the Middle East and endangers the security of supply
in the world, citizens are advised to use fuel carefully and efficiently.
The Energy and Water Utilities Regulatory Authority (EWURA) hereby publish Cap
Prices for petroleum products, applicable in Tanzania Mainland, effective from
Wednesday, 6th May 2026 at 12:01 am. In May 2026, the retail and wholesale prices
of petroleum products in Dar es Salaam, Tanga, and Mtwara are depicted in Tables
1 and 2, respectively.
